purpose: Test whether width256 with one recurrent layer preserves the useful d256 contribution at lower measured streaming cost.

recipe.parent: Exact original d256 EMA/since/distillation recipe, with layers changed from 2 to 1 only; fixed 4 epochs, select model_ep3.
recipe.teachers: Same-fold original plain h256 seed3 and seed4 prediction mean; historical logical IDs h256_f{fold},h256s4_f{fold}; not a d256 distilled teacher.
recipe.head: Ordinary existing H2 recipe from own same-fold parent ep3; freeze inp and gru, two epochs, fixed model_ep1; no distillation.

primary.question: Preserved forecast contribution versus measured cost reduction, replacing only d256.

secondary.candidate: Exactly the same candidate fixed4 as primary.
secondary.question: Competition utility versus operational fixed3; no composition or blend search.

comparisons.anchor_lineage: Reuse exact existing same-fold d256 parent4-to-H2 anchors and unchanged H2 partner anchors; bind endpoint hashes before allocation.

source_estimates.runtime_inference: MAC counts are not runtime measurements. Dense candidate fixed4 can still be too slow; quantized serving is a separate prospective numerical candidate.

limitations: Same seed with different layer count does not guarantee identical initialization RNG consumption or sampler order; this is a recipe screen, not a clean causal depth ablation.
